summary: CONMED Corporation filed an 8-K reporting it entered into privately negotiated purchase agreements to buy back approximately $645.2 million aggregate principal amount of its 2.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 for about $637.2 million in cash, implying a price per note of ~98.76% of par. The purchase price includes no premium, consistent with a debt repurchase. The transactions are expected to close on June 15, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. This is an issuer tender for its own convertible notes, reducing leverage and potential equity dilution. What to watch: whether remaining noteholders force conversion or the company pursues further liability management.
